messages:
liv: Heads-up — we just got a support escalation from ACME: p95 and p99 for /v1/chat jumped ~3-4x starting ~22:10 UTC. Customer saw long tails and a few 503s. Ticket #INC-9876.
sam: Ugh. Any correlation with deploys or config changes around that time?
jess: No code deploys in prod at 22:10. We had a config push to routing + a small prefix canonicalization change rolled at 21:55 — that touched how we canonicalize header keys before computing prefix cache keys. Could be related.
maurice: Can we get kv/prefix cache metrics? Miss rate, evictions, hotkey spikes?
ade: Pulling metrics now. cloudwatch query looks bad: prefix_cache.miss_rate p95 jumped from 4% -> 28% around 22:05. Eviction count spiked too. KV memory usage stayed flat.
liv: So sounds like entropy in key space increased post-canonicalize and multiplied distinct prefix keys -> warmup + eviction thrash.
oncall-bot: Alert: prefix-cache-eviction-rate high for service=runtime at 22:08 (threshold breached)
sam: Repro steps — can we simulate traffic with header variations? Maybe a customer is sending dynamic header values (session-id/token) and canonicalization now includes something that previously was stripped.
jess: I found the PR: #1428 — it started preserving `x-tenant-region` in prefix fingerprint instead of normalizing to `region`. If tenant header has high cardinality, that explains the entropy.
maurice: Nice catch. Quick mitigation options:
- rollback canonicalization change (fastest)
- add normalization to drop high-cardinality tenant-specific fields from prefix key
- increase cache capacity (stopgap)
- enable warmup drip to avoid eviction storms
liv: For now, can we flip a feature-flag to revert to old canonicalization? How risky is rollback?
ade: Feature flag exists in config service; flipping is low-risk. But need to coordinate with routing so no partial rollouts. I can do a full flip in 5m.
sam: While flipping, throttle upstream to give cache time to warm up? Maybe apply a short global concurrency cap for that customer.
jess: Also suggest adding a short-lived circuit-breaker on warmup: if miss_rate > 15% and evictions > X, force local backoff and route to fallback model to protect latency.
liv: Action items:
- ade: flip canonicalization flag -> revert preservation of x-tenant-region (ETA 5m)
- sam: put temp concurrency cap on ACME route (ETA 10m)
- maurice: prepare a short diff to explicitly strip tenant headers from prefix key in next deploy
- jess: add safe-guard rule to console to detect sudden key-cardinality spikes
- support-bot: update ticket INC-9876 with mitigation plan
support-bot: Ticket INC-9876 updated: rollback canonicalization + rate-limit applied. Monitoring p95/p99.
ade: Flag flipped at 22:18 UTC. Observability: prefix_cache.miss_rate p95 started falling within 2m.
maurice: Eviction rate decreased, p95 dropped ~55% and p99 trending down. Still watching.
sam: Will follow up with a proper postmortem and suggested permanent fix (strip tenant-specific fields at key derivation, add warmup-drip by default for new prefixes).
jess: Repro notes for postmortem:
1) Start with baseline traffic replay for customer X
2) Generate header permutations with dynamic x-tenant-region values (thousands of uniques)
3) Observe cache key cardinality via `prefix_stats.top_keys` and eviction delta
4) Validate mitigation by enabling normalization and comparing miss/eviction curves
Example CLI to stress:
```
for i in {1..5000}; do curl -s -H "x-tenant-region: r-$i" https://api.redwood/v1/chat?model=fast > /dev/null &
done
```
liv: Good. Also add automated detection: alert when top-100 prefix cardinality exceeds baseline by 10x.
ade: Closing loop: customer confirmed latency improved and removed escalation. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and then mark resolved in ticket.
maurice: I'll open a follow-up issue to harden prefix key derivation and add unit tests covering header normalization.
liv: Thanks everyone. Great triage and quick rollback. :thumbsup:
